A1.justification: The title, authors, method, and main experiments match, and all ten pages of each PDF are readable. Both end with references despite referring to an appendix for additional results, analyses, and failure cases; that material is unavailable for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-editing comparisons on PIE in Table 1, iteration ablations in Table 2, and qualitative experimental results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original PIE comparisons, iteration ablations, and qualitative image-editing results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations 9–12 retain fixed-point inversion with averaging, velocity compensation, and token-aware AdaLN feature replacement. Expanded motivation and the shared-timestep disclosure do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both report evaluation on the same 700-image PIE benchmark and retain the same illustrated editing coverage, including replacement, style, quantity, pose, shape, facial expression, and visual text. No additional dataset or task scenario is reported.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 6 retain PnP, P2P, MasaCtrl, InsP2P, and InfEdit, with the same displayed inversion pairings. Figure 3 retains the Euler/SD3.5 versus DDIM/SD1.5 comparison.

E3.justification: Both specify 30 inversion steps, CFG values 1 and 2, and three fixed-point iterations for the proposed method; diffusion baselines retain 50 steps and CFG 7. Metrics and the 150-image ablation sample are unchanged. Sharing S across editing types is newly disclosed, without an explicit protocol revision.

E4.justification: The available iteration, injection-duration, and reconstruction analyses in Table 2 and Figures 5, 7, and 8 match. Both defer detailed attention-component analyses, velocity-compensation results, and failure cases to an absent appendix, preventing comparison of those supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates. Both numerical tables retain point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 are numerically identical, including Table 1's proposed-method PSNR of 26.62 and CLIP scores of 25.74 and 22.27. Displayed qualitative examples also match. The additional non-rigid numerical results attributed to the missing appendix cannot be compared.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and the mathematical development of rectified flow, Euler/DDIM inversion, fixed-point iteration, and compensation are retained. No formal definition, derivation, assumption, or proof is substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about inversion error, two-stage inversion, and AdaLN control supporting rigid and non-rigid editing. The revised conclusion preserves their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 explicitly connects the inversion rationale to avoiding image-only overfitting and preserving text-image alignment. Figure 5's caption qualifies interference as possible hindrance to sitting-to-standing editing. The stated out-of-domain and computational limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link on page 1 and explicitly states in Section 5 that the injection timestep S is shared across editing types. These improve access information and setting disclosure; the PDFs do not establish the linked site's code availability.

R1.justification: The bibliography removes eight distinct works, including Flow Matching for Generative Modeling, SiT, T2I-Adapter, and IP-Adapter, plus a duplicate DiT entry. These entries were not cited in v1's supplied main text; the substantive related-work discussion and research positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized rewrites in the motivation, experiment introduction, limitations, impact paragraph, and conclusion, and corrects some spelling and heading capitalization. The section sequence and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves from page 5 to page 6, with accompanying movement of Algorithm 1 and surrounding text. Figure 5's caption is refined. The same eight figures and two tables remain, without substantive redesign or changed table structure.

improvement.justification: The shared-S disclosure, project-page pointer, and clearer inversion rationale provide a limited improvement in documentation and accessibility. The visible empirical support is unchanged, and the appendix material promised by both versions remains unavailable, limiting the overall gain.
